## Why This Is Asked
Designing a prefetch-aware I/O scheduler tests practical trade-offs between locality and fairness in a concrete, testable path from submission to completion.

## Key Concepts
- I/O scheduling and read-ahead
- locality-aware prefetch policies
- starvation prevention and fairness
- per-device queues and a simple ring-buffer implementation

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal sketch for a per-device ring queue
typedef struct { int block; int next; } BlockNode;
typedef struct { BlockNode ring[64]; int head; int tail; } DeviceQueue;
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend the policy for multiple devices with shared bandwidth?
- How would you evaluate latency, throughput, and starvation in a test harness?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical OS I/O scheduling knowledge, device heterogeneity, and fairness under mixed workloads. It requires concrete data structures and a concrete scheduling policy.

## Key Concepts
- Block I/O scheduling and per-device queues
- Priority-aware fairness across heterogeneous devices
- Read/write path optimization and deadline vs throughput trade-offs
- Data structures: per-device heaps/queues, per-process weights

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-C-like sketch
typedef struct IOReq { int pid; int type; int prio; int deadline; int addr; int len; } IOReq;
typedef struct DeviceQueue { Heap reads; Heap writes; int device_id; } DeviceQueue;
IOReq* pick_next(DeviceQueue* dq) { /* if has reads, pop min by deadline; else pop writes by addr */ }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate fairness under bursty mixed workloads?
- How to adjust dynamically when SSD queue depth changes or new devices hot-plugged?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests understanding of crash-consistency mechanisms, journaling design patterns, and recovery strategies in filesystems. It evaluates how candidates ensure atomic metadata updates and maintain data integrity across power failures.

## Key Concepts
- Write-ahead logging (WAL) and journaling principles
- Two-phase commit protocols for atomic operations
- Recovery procedures and log replay semantics
- Fsync semantics and write ordering guarantees
- Crash scenario handling and partial write detection

## Code Example
```c
typedef struct {
    uint64_t lsn;     // Log sequence number
    uint32_t op;      // Operation type (create, delete, etc.)
    uint32_t ino;     // Inode number
    uint32_t parent;  // Parent directory inode
} log_entry_t;

void log_append(log_entry_t *entries, size_t count);
void log_commit(uint64_t lsn);
```
